content.key_idea: The QCCD architecture connects 1D ion traps through 4-way junctions so ions can be shuttled and collectively swapped, letting two ions be brought into one trap to perform a two-qubit CNOT gate.
content.reading_order: panel (a) top-left shows the overall collective swap of ion pairs (1,3) and (2,4); panels (b)-(e), boxed at top-right, break that swap into individual shuttle steps; panel (f), bottom-left, shows the resulting CNOT gates once ions share a trap.

summary: This figure illustrates the QCCD (quantum charge-coupled device) architecture that iSwitch builds on, not iSwitch's own contribution. Panel (a) shows a 2D grid of 1D ion traps connected by 4-way junctions, with orange arrows tracing a collective shuttle that swaps ion pairs (1,3) and (2,4). Panels (b)-(e), grouped in a dashed box, break this collective swap into four individual shuttle steps between traps and junctions. Panel (f) shows the outcome: once shuttled ions share a trap, a two-qubit CNOT gate (marked by a red dotted oval) can be executed on them. A legend at the bottom defines the trap, junction, ion qubit, vacant spot, shuttle-arrow, and CNOT-gate symbols used throughout.
